- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs."

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd

💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart
final registryCwd = registry?[id]?['cwd'];
```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart
final entry = registry?[id];
final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

A regression test with a non-map registry entry (no spawn needed, `MemoryExecutionEnv` suffices) would pin it.

`agent_cli_inbox.dart:419`:

if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

Two observations:

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.

| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`).     "description": "Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs."
  }

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. - **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: registry entry shape is unguarded in `directory()` — a non-map entry crashes the whole listing**

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart
final registryCwd = registry?[id]?['cwd'];
```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

A regression test with a non-map registry entry (no spawn needed, `MemoryExecutionEnv` suffices) would pin it.

`agent_cli_inbox.dart:419`:

if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

Two observations:

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.
2. `FileKind` is documented as pi's semantics: *"Symlinks are not followed automatically."* On any backend honoring that (lstat), **symlink→file** would pass this check and then die with the raw `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — the exact failure mode gh-1744 exists to prevent.

Neither blocks the merge (current hosts behave correctly), but the doc comment's "`Directory(cwd).existsSync()` semantics … symlinks stay allowed" overstates the guarantee. Consider resolving the link (`fileInfo` on the target) or scoping the comment, and note why the arm exists — there is currently no test exercising it (the memory env cannot produce `symlink`).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a second, undocumented legacy-slug ambiguity class flips decode**

`session_repo.dart:174` — the reversible marker is "slug contains a recognized `%XX` escape". That detection also catches **legacy on-disk slugs** whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text. Verified against this diff's decoder:

| legacy on-disk slug | decode before this PR | decode after |
|---|---|---|
| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs."

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. - **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `FileKind.symlink` arm is unreachable on every current backend, and on lstat-semantics backends it re-opens the bug being fixed**

if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

Two observations:

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);

if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs."

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

{
  "key": "pr-1751",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names",
    "description": "Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs."
  }
}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;

```

| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +594
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:04:00Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- Every Windows path changes slug too: `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so `C:\Users\...` encodes as `--C%3A-Users-...--` instead of legacy `--C-Users-...--` — the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory and old slug folders coexist (any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is picked up again once that session re-registers).
- A second legacy ambiguity class: legacy slugs whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text (`%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`) now unescape on decode instead of staying literal; bounded to the `directory()` cwd fallback, which the registry's exact cwd overrides and `launchMailboxWake` refuses by name when wrong.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart
final entry = registry?[id];
final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)

`agent_cli_inbox.dart:419`:

if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

Two observations:

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)

    12	      .replaceAll('-', '%2D')

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …
